body.p: , after , , , , , , , . sxml follows xsi:schemaLocation and xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation when the host asks for it (XSD 1.1 Part 1, 4.3.2: "Schema processors should provide an option to control whether they do so").

item.p: API (additive, schema.h; no substrate header changes): one field at the end of sxml_schema_configuration, sxml_item schema_location_hint_node. The zero item is today's behaviour. A document, element or attribute node names the instance: after the configured documents and everything they refer to, every hint of the node's subtree, in document order, is asked of the processor's resolver (kind SCHEMA_DOCUMENT, the location resolved against the base URI of the attribute's element, the hinted namespace as target_namespace_uri) and read with what it refers to before the next hint is weighed. No new resource kind, no file access of the library's own: what the resolver delivers is the trust rule, as for xs:import.

Why on the schema, not the validator. Part 1, 4.1: an incremental assembly "must result in an assessment outcome that is the same as would be given if assessment were undertaken again with the final, fully assembled schema", and 4.3.2: hints on any element have a global effect. A validator that added documents while it validates could not promise that for content it already assessed; collecting the hints of the whole instance first and assembling one schema does, and it is the existing reader and assembly (src/schema_assemble.c: a hint is one more RESOLVED document in the work list; relation HINT, reported in itself as a configured document). A streaming host that wants hints parses the instance once to collect them (sxml validate does: two parses).

When a hint is ignored (4.3.2, strategy 1 "do nothing ... a schema containing components for the given namespace name is already known"): when a document already read has the hinted namespace as target namespace (the configured schema, an earlier hint or what it imported), and for the XML Schema and XML Schema instance namespaces. So hints only add namespaces; they never replace, extend or redefine the configured ones. This is also XSLT 4.0, 25.1.3's rule for hints ("must not override or redefine any schema components in the static context") and keeps 4.3.2's security note: a document cannot swap the schema of a namespace the host chose. A namespace without a location is ignored; a document the resolver does not deliver is no error ("It is not an error for such an attempt to fail"); a delivered one with another target namespace than its hint's is (as a document that is not a schema document), and errors of hinted documents fail the compilation as configured ones do.

The languages. fn:xsd-validator with use-xsi-schema-location=true (F&O 4.0, 17.2.5) compiles its options' documents with the target's hints; with no documents option, the hints' schema comes after the in-scope schemas, so that an in-scope declaration wins. A failure of the hints (a document that is not a schema, a conflict) makes V return is-valid false with the error in error-details, "an invalidity, not a dynamic error" (17.2.5); FODC0009 for the option is gone. fn:doc, fn:doc-available, fn:parse-xml and XSLT's fn:document with use-xsi-schema-location=true (F&O 4.0, 17.1.1, 17.2.1; XSLT 4.0, 20.1) validate against the in-scope schemas and then a schema of the document's hints. XQuery's validate expression keeps use-xsi-schema-location=false (XQuery 4.0, 4.25 recommends it) and XSLT validation attributes ignore hints (XSLT 4.0, 25.1.3 leaves it implementation-defined).

sxml validate gets the flag --use-schema-location (: an explicit flag, never a mode guessed from the input or from a missing option; like sxml check --external-entities, it opts in to reading files a FILE names): each FILE's hints, relative to the FILE (standard input: the working directory), are read as local files through the CLI's resolver, never the network, and assembled with the --schema documents into the schema of that FILE. --schema is required unless the flag is given. A FILE is parsed twice then, once for its hints; errors of a hinted document are reported as schema errors of that FILE (DOCUMENT:LINE:COLUMN: CONSTRAINT: description, in JSON in its errors with document) and make it invalid.

xlink.xsd ('s introspection set): the W3C's http://www.w3.org/XML/2008/06/xlink.xsd is vendored in third_party/w3c-xlink/ with its license (W3C Software and Document License) and served by the XSD driver's resolver for that URI, as the library serves its stand-in xml.xsd; the introspection set is run.

The XSD driver follows hints through the library now (its own scan of xsi:schemaLocation pairs is gone): an instance with a hint attribute compiles the test's documents again with schema_location_hint_node, used when it compiles, as before.
QT4 driver: the feature schema-location-hint ("at" hints of import schema resolved as relative URIs) is supported for XQuery; qischema041, 042 and 083 pass.
